_doc: Binaries shipped with the installer next to the server (SPEC-v3 V7, brief 1: resources/bin). Every entry needs name, version, license (SPDX expression) and source. Pinned downloads (url, sha256) and the build steps live in desktop/packaging/third-party.json and desktop/scripts/stage.js; keep both files in step. stage.js fails the build when the ffmpeg configure line contains --enable-gpl or --enable-nonfree. aria2c (SPEC-ext) is GPL-2.0-or-later with an OpenSSL linking permission (note): a separate program LectureFlow starts in RPC mode, not linked into it; source_code lists where the corresponding source of ffmpeg and aria2c is: first the release attachment that desktop/scripts/sources.js builds for every release (the pinned upstream tarballs, unchanged, with our build scripts), then the upstream addresses of the same files; resources/licenses/{ffmpeg,aria2}/SOURCE.txt names the attachment of that version.

binaries.name: ffmpeg / ffprobe (Windows build)
binaries.note: Built by desktop/scripts/build-ffmpeg-windows.sh (Linux, mingw-w64 GCC win32 thread model; Docker image and toolchain versions pinned in desktop/packaging/third-party.json) with exactly the configure line above: no GPL, no non-free, no version3, no autodetected libraries. Shared DLLs (avcodec, avformat, avfilter, avdevice, avutil, swscale, swresample) next to ffmpeg.exe and ffprobe.exe, so they can be replaced; the build checks that they import only Windows system DLLs and each other. External code inside: listed under bundled (OpenH264, libvpl and dav1d in avcodec, zlib, NVENC headers; GCC and MinGW-w64 runtime parts linked statically). Licence texts ship in resources/licenses/ffmpeg (with BUILDINFO.txt). NVENC needs an NVIDIA driver 531.61 or newer. Corresponding source: attached to every LectureFlow release on GitHub, next to the installers, as LectureFlow-<version>-source-ffmpeg-windows-x64.tar (the pinned FFmpeg, zlib, nv-codec-headers, OpenH264, libvpl and dav1d tarballs, unchanged, with desktop/scripts/build-ffmpeg-windows.sh and its pins); resources/licenses/ffmpeg/SOURCE.txt names the attachment of that version. The other addresses in its corresponding-source list are upstream's, for reference. The GCC and MinGW-w64 runtime sources are not attached: the GCC Runtime Library Exception 3.1 and the ZPL-2.1 ask for none; their Ubuntu source packages are listed.

bundled.name: OpenH264
bundled.note: H.264 encoder (libopenh264) in avcodec, compiled from source; Cisco's patent coverage applies only to Cisco's own binaries.

bundled.name: libvpl (Intel Video Processing Library dispatcher)
bundled.note: Intel Quick Sync (h264_qsv) in avcodec; loads the Intel runtime from the driver at run time.

bundled.name: dav1d
bundled.note: AV1 software decoder (libdav1d) linked statically into avcodec, built from the pinned 1.5.4 release tarball with meson. COPYING and the AOMedia Patent License 1.0 (doc/PATENTS) ship in resources/licenses/ffmpeg.

bundled.name: nv-codec-headers
bundled.note: Headers only (NVENC, h264_nvenc); the NVIDIA driver is loaded at run time.

bundled.name: GCC runtime libraries (libgcc, libstdc++)
bundled.note: Linked statically (-static-libgcc; libstdc++ for OpenH264 and libvpl). The GCC Runtime Library Exception 3.1 exempts the compiled program from the GPL: no GPL obligations attach to ffmpeg.

bundled.name: MinGW-w64 runtime (static CRT parts)
bundled.note: Startup code and libmingwex helpers linked statically; some files are public domain. The C runtime itself is msvcrt.dll from Windows.

binaries.name: ffmpeg / ffprobe (macOS build)
binaries.note: Built by desktop/scripts/build-ffmpeg-macos.sh with exactly the configure line above. Static executables; the one third-party library inside is dav1d (bundled), linked statically. zlib, VideoToolbox and AudioToolbox are system libraries of macOS, linked dynamically; the build checks that nothing else is. Built for macOS 13.0 or later (the app's minimum). Corresponding source: attached to every LectureFlow release on GitHub, next to the installers, as LectureFlow-<version>-source-ffmpeg-darwin-arm64.tar (the pinned ffmpeg-9.0.2.tar.xz and dav1d-1.5.4.tar.xz, unchanged, with that build script and its pins); resources/licenses/ffmpeg/SOURCE.txt names the attachment of that version. The other addresses in its corresponding-source list are upstream's, for reference.

bundled.name: dav1d
bundled.note: AV1 software decoder (libdav1d) linked statically into ffmpeg and ffprobe, built from the pinned 1.5.4 release tarball with meson. COPYING and the AOMedia Patent License 1.0 (doc/PATENTS) ship in resources/licenses/ffmpeg.

binaries.name: uv
binaries.note: Creates the component virtual environments (SPEC-v3 V3.1). LICENSE-MIT and LICENSE-APACHE of the 0.13.1 tag ship in resources/licenses/uv.

binaries.name: aria2c (Windows build)
binaries.note: Download tool of the browser extension's download queue (SPEC-ext), started by LectureFlow in RPC mode only. aria2 is under the GNU GPL version 2 or later with an additional permission to link with OpenSSL (COPYING, LICENSE.OpenSSL and the source file headers). Neither bundled build links OpenSSL: Windows uses WinTLS (SChannel), macOS AppleTLS (Security.framework). A separate program that LectureFlow starts and talks to over JSON-RPC; it is not linked into LectureFlow. The binary is upstream's own Windows build, used unchanged and pinned by the SHA-256 of the zip and of aria2c.exe (desktop/packaging/third-party.json); upstream's build scripts are Dockerfile.mingw and mingw-config in the 1.37.0 source tarball. Statically linked (README.mingw): GMP, Expat, SQLite, zlib, c-ares, libssh2, the WebSocket library wslay from the aria2 source, and the static parts of the GCC and MinGW-w64 runtimes; it imports only Windows system DLLs. Enabled features: Async DNS, BitTorrent, Firefox3 Cookie, GZip, HTTPS (WinTLS; TLS 1.3 does not work, README.mingw), Message Digest, Metalink, XML-RPC, SFTP. LectureFlow uses only HTTP(S) downloads over JSON-RPC. Corresponding source: attached to every LectureFlow release on GitHub, next to the installers, as LectureFlow-<version>-source-aria2c-windows-x64.tar (the aria2 1.37.0 source with upstream's Dockerfile.mingw and mingw-config, and the pinned GMP, Expat, SQLite, zlib, c-ares and libssh2 tarballs, unchanged); resources/licenses/aria2/SOURCE.txt names the attachment of that version. The other addresses in its corresponding-source list are upstream's, for reference. The GCC and MinGW-w64 runtime sources are not attached: the GCC Runtime Library Exception 3.1 and the ZPL-2.1 ask for none; their Ubuntu source packages are listed. COPYING, LICENSE.OpenSSL, AUTHORS, README.mingw, SOURCE.txt and the libraries' license texts ship in resources/licenses/aria2.

bundled.name: GMP
bundled.note: Multi-precision arithmetic (BitTorrent key exchange). Statically linked by upstream's build.

bundled.name: Expat
bundled.note: XML parser (Metalink, XML-RPC). Statically linked by upstream's build.

bundled.name: SQLite
bundled.note: Reads Firefox 3 / Chromium cookie files (--load-cookies); public-domain dedication, no license text required. Statically linked by upstream's build.

bundled.name: zlib
bundled.note: gzip content encoding. Statically linked by upstream's build.

bundled.name: c-ares
bundled.note: Asynchronous DNS. Statically linked by upstream's build.

bundled.name: libssh2
bundled.note: SFTP downloads. Statically linked by upstream's build.

bundled.name: wslay
bundled.note: WebSocket library of aria2's RPC interface, compiled in from the aria2 source; its COPYING ships in resources/licenses/aria2/thirdparty.

bundled.name: GCC runtime libraries (libgcc, libstdc++)
bundled.note: Linked statically by upstream's build. The GCC Runtime Library Exception 3.1 exempts the compiled program from the GPL-3.0 terms of these libraries (COPYING.RUNTIME ships in resources/licenses/aria2/thirdparty).

bundled.name: MinGW-w64 runtime (static CRT parts)
bundled.note: Startup code and libmingwex helpers linked statically by upstream's build; some files are public domain. The C runtime itself is msvcrt.dll from Windows. COPYING.MinGW-w64-runtime.txt ships in resources/licenses/aria2/thirdparty.

binaries.name: aria2c (macOS build)
binaries.note: Download tool of the browser extension's download queue (SPEC-ext), started by LectureFlow in RPC mode only. aria2 is under the GNU GPL version 2 or later with an additional permission to link with OpenSSL (COPYING, LICENSE.OpenSSL and the source file headers). Neither bundled build links OpenSSL: Windows uses WinTLS (SChannel), macOS AppleTLS (Security.framework). A separate program that LectureFlow starts and talks to over JSON-RPC; it is not linked into LectureFlow. Built by packaging/aria2c/build-aria2c-macos.sh with exactly the configure line above, for macOS 13.0 or later (the app's minimum). AppleTLS (Security.framework; certificates are checked against the system trust store); OpenSSL, GnuTLS, nettle, GMP, libgcrypt, libxml2, Expat, SQLite, libssh2, c-ares, BitTorrent and Metalink are off. Linked dynamically only to macOS system libraries (libz, libc++, libiconv, libSystem, CoreFoundation, Security); the build checks otool -L, the minimum macOS version and aria2c --version. The one third-party library inside is wslay (WebSocket, MIT), part of the aria2 source. Corresponding source: attached to every LectureFlow release on GitHub, next to the installers, as LectureFlow-<version>-source-aria2c-darwin-arm64.tar (the pinned aria2-1.37.0.tar.xz, unchanged, with that build script and its pins); resources/licenses/aria2/SOURCE.txt names the attachment of that version. The other addresses in its corresponding-source list are upstream's, for reference. COPYING, LICENSE.OpenSSL, AUTHORS, BUILDINFO.txt, SOURCE.txt and wslay's COPYING ship in resources/licenses/aria2.

bundled.name: wslay
bundled.note: WebSocket library of aria2's RPC interface, compiled in from the aria2 source; its COPYING ships in resources/licenses/aria2/thirdparty.
